page: Microsoft Azure E8-4ds_v6 is an Edsv6 family virtual machine configured with 4 vCPUs and 2 physical Intel Xeon 8573C cores operating at 4.2 GHz. Built on the x86_64 architecture and running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor, this instance features 64.0 GB of RAM, equating to 16.0 GB of memory per core. The processor includes a 260 MB L3 cache and supports advanced instruction sets, including Advanced Vector Extensions (AVX-512) and Advanced Matrix Extensions (AMX) for accelerated vector and matrix operations. Local storage is provided via a 472 GB NVMe SSD.

Performance benchmarks reveal a contrast between single-core and multi-core capabilities. The server demonstrates strong single-core performance, evidenced by a Geekbench single-core score of 2170.0 and a single-threaded gzip compression speed of 31.35 GB/sec. However, multi-core and memory bandwidth metrics are more constrained. The stress-ng multi-core CPU performance is rated as weak at 3990.17, and the uncached large-block memory read bandwidth is also weak at 37.14 GB/sec. Database operations, such as Redis SET, show lower throughput at 5.71 million operations per second, while static web serving achieves an average throughput of 7.8 GB/sec.

From a resource density perspective, the E8-4ds_v6 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio of 16 GB per vCPU, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-bound workloads that do not require massive parallel CPU scaling. The primary tradeoff lies in its limited physical core count (2 cores), which restricts multi-threaded performance and heavy computational compilation tasks. This server is best suited for memory-intensive applications, small-to-medium database hosting, caching layers, and lightweight text or image processing tasks that benefit from high memory capacity and strong single-core execution.
